title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
summary: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. title: No sanctions and no recrimination: Cricket Australia ball tampering forum to include 2017-18 Ashes series
summary: Scope of forum includes Australia’s entire 2017-18 season Independent process to be led by senior counsel Fiona McLeod The scope of a forum set up to provide Australian players and staff on the 2018 tour of South Africa with an opportunity to air their views on sandpapergate has been broadened to include experiences from the 2017-18 Ashes series. Cricket Australia (CA) on Friday revealed the terms under which those who want to can share their experiences in a “safe and confidential” environment, after the ball tampering saga blew up again following the publication of Usman Khawaja’s memoir earlier this month. title: Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua: Paris Fury retracts claim her husband was diagnosed with schizophrenia
summary: Paris Fury had told new documentary about condition Disclosure had put Joshua fight at risk of cancellation Paris Fury has retracted her suggestion that her husband, the boxer Tyson Fury, was diagnosed with schizophrenia just months after beating Wladimir Klitschko to win the world heavyweight title in Düsseldorf in November 2015. Paris Fury made the remark in an initial version of a Netflix documentary which will be released on Friday. Netflix said it has worked to “update” the footage in light of her clarification.
